title: Quentin and the Verdict
premise: When Ada Iversen, archivist of St. Brannoc's Cathedral, discovers that the diary of Marion Quill — a missing woman declared dead twelve years ago — contains entries written after her disappearance, she realizes the town's verdict was a lie sealed inside the crypt she alone can open. Following the diary's trail of coded references to parish records, Ada uncovers a conspiracy among the town's founding families who staged Marion's death to bury what she witnessed. As the anniversary trial that legitimized the cover-up approaches, Ada must decide whether to trust the estranged Quill family and a disgraced former constable, risking her own erasure from the records. In the end, Ada opens the crypt before the town, exposes the living conspirators at the trial, and gives Marion's found family — the misfits who loved her — the justice the law refused.
about_author: Ulyana Galloway is a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing the quiet cruelties of small towns before turning them into fiction. She writes mysteries about people the paperwork forgot, from a farmhouse full of rescued cats and unreliable typewriters.

chapters.title: The Alphabet of Absence
chapters.summary: Ada Iversen's POV. Establishes her ordered life in the cathedral archive, her ritual of filing the town's secrets, and the locked crypt she has never entered in twelve years. Emotional beat: contentment built on avoidance, cracked by an unexplained gap in the 2012 ledger.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Ada finds Marion Quill's donated diary in a bequest box and discovers entries dated months after the official date of her disappearance. Her hands shake as she reads a line addressed to 'whoever keeps the files.' Emotional beat: vertigo — the foundation of her ordered world splits.

chapters.title: The Verdict Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada walks the town on the eve of the twelfth-anniversary memorial, noting how everyone repeats the same rehearsed story of Marion's drowning. Flashbacks establish the trial that closed the case. Emotional beat: unease at how smoothly grief has been choreographed.

chapters.title: A Constable Without a Badge
chapters.summary: Ada seeks out Deshawn Pike, the constable dismissed after questioning the drowning verdict. He initially refuses her, bitter and drinking, until she reads him the post-disappearance entries aloud. Emotional beat: two exiles recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Crypt Keeps
chapters.summary: Ada attempts the crypt door and finds the lock changed — keys held only by the cathedral board, chaired by Aldous Vane, the trial's lead benefactor. Someone has been inside recently; the dust is disturbed. Emotional beat: first concrete evidence of a living conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Signed
chapters.summary: Marion's sister Ruth Quill arrives for the memorial, cold and hostile, insisting the family wants no reopening. But Ada notices Ruth's signature on the bequest that delivered the diary to the archive — a deliberate act. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into denial.

chapters.title: Coded in the Margins
chapters.summary: Deshawn and Ada decode Marion's margin symbols against old parish registers, mapping her final weeks: she had discovered financial irregularities tying Vane's family to the crypt's contents. Emotional beat: the thrill of partnership rekindling Ada's frozen heart.

chapters.title: Someone Reads Over Your Shoulder
chapters.summary: The archive is searched overnight; pages are razored from the 2012 register. Ada realizes whoever took them knew exactly which file — meaning someone inside the church. Emotional beat: paranoia; her sanctuary becomes a trap.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Left Flowers
chapters.summary: A teenage boy, Theo, admits he has left flowers at the crypt door every week for years — taught by a woman he calls his aunt, whom readers recognize as Marion alive. He gives Ada a note he was told to deliver 'when someone finally asked.' Emotional beat: hope arriving sideways through a child.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Ruth breaks: she has known Marion lived, protected by silence because Vane threatened to prosecute Ruth's son for the staged accident. She reveals the crypt holds not a body but the ledger proving the fraud. Emotional beat: guilt transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Board Convenes
chapters.summary: Vane moves to have Ada removed as archivist on fabricated grounds of record tampering, forcing her to watch allies on the board look away. She copies the surviving files and hides them in plain sight among hymnal catalogs. Emotional beat: the machinery of respectability grinding down.

chapters.title: Night Shift at the Necropolis
chapters.summary: Deshawn stakes out the crypt and photographs Vane's lawyer entering after midnight with fresh documents — they are destroying evidence ahead of the anniversary trial's ceremonial reaffirmation. Emotional beat: dread with a deadline now attached.

chapters.title: The Woman in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: Ada follows Theo's directions and finally meets Marion Quill — alive, weathered, unrepentant, hiding in the decommissioned tower. Marion explains why she let the town mourn her rather than fight men who owned every judge. Emotional beat: fury and awe; the ghost is flesh.

chapters.title: Why She Let Them Bury Her
chapters.summary: Marion's account: she saw the crypt used to store payoffs and a child's remains from an older crime; testifying meant death, so she chose symbolic death instead. She refuses to return, believing the town deserves its comfortable lie. Emotional beat: Ada confronting the cost of survival versus justice.

chapters.title: Found Family, Assembled
chapters.summary: Ada gathers the unlikely coalition — Ruth, Deshawn, Theo, and the cathedral's aging verger who kept silent out of fear — in the archive after hours. They plan to open the crypt publicly during the anniversary service. Emotional beat: warmth kindling in a cold case; the theme made explicit.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Stacks
chapters.summary: The verger confesses under pressure to Vane that Ada has Marion; Vane's men ransack the tower, but Marion has already slipped away, leaving a message: 'Open it yourself.' Theo goes missing briefly, raising stakes. Emotional beat: betrayal, then relief, then steel.

chapters.title: Keys and Consequences
chapters.summary: Deshawn uses his old warrant knowledge to legally compel the crypt's opening, exploiting a procedural flaw Vane's own lawyer created. The board fractures; one member defects with a duplicate key. Emotional beat: the law, bent back toward justice.

chapters.title: The Opening
chapters.summary: Before the assembled congregation at the anniversary service, Ada turns the key. Inside: no coffin, but the hidden ledger, payoff records, and the small coffin of the long-buried child. Gasps; Vane rises to denounce forgery. Emotional beat: terrible vindication.

chapters.title: Trial by Congregation
chapters.summary: Marion walks into the cathedral mid-service, alive and named, dismantling Vane's defense with testimony the original trial never heard. The defected board member corroborates. Vane's arrest is not tidy but is real. Emotional beat: catharsis; justice outside the law converging with law itself.

chapters.title: What We Do With the Dead
chapters.summary: The child's remains are buried properly, named at last, with the whole town forced to attend its own reckoning. Ruth and Marion grieve together for the first time in twelve years. Emotional beat: mourning that is finally honest.

chapters.title: Recatalogued
chapters.summary: Ada rebuilds the archive, adding a new section for truths previously unfiled, and declines offers to leave — the town needs an honest keeper more than a discreet one. Deshawn is reinstated. Emotional beat: quiet restoration.

chapters.title: The Diary's Last Entry
chapters.summary: Marion gives Ada the diary's true final page, written that morning: an entry about coming home, filed alphabetically under 'Q' where it always belonged. The found family shares supper in the archive. Emotional beat: belonging, earned and archived.
